body.prompt:
Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L02_E, a close three-quarter view of the Food Street dosa dispenser set up for a cold test: the measuring cup swung aside on its hinge and a trial bowl on the cold cooking plate under the spout.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate L02_D of this same dispenser. Use it for: the exact design of the brass tank with its narrow inspection window, the supply tap, the measuring cup with its scale strip and stop clip, the long wood-gripped handle, the guarded iron cooking plate and heater switch; materials and light. Keep every fitting's shape identical; only the states below change.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master, for finish only. Ignore: all white label boxes, annotation words and arrows; cart, bowls, trolley, table.
Camera and framing: close three-quarter view from the cool customer side, outside the counter, standing eye height looking slightly down. The entrance end is frame-left. In frame: the tank's lower body with its inspection window (top edge cuts the tank), the supply tap and spout at upper centre, the complete cup hinge, the long handle, and the round cooking plate in the lower centre. The cream front edge and blue timber joint are visible. The angle shows the bowl's inside and the space directly under the spout.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Measuring cup: swung out towards frame-right (the Parade end) on its cleaning hinge, which stays visibly fixed to the right-hand tank support leg; the cup is empty and hangs supported by the hinge; its wooden-grip outer bracket faces the camera.
2. Spout: now exposed, directly above the centre of the cooking plate.
3. Trial bowl: one small brass bowl resting flat on the cooking plate directly below the spout, with a shallow layer of pale cream batter in it.
4. Supply tap: CLOSED. A clear dry gap of air between the spout tip and the bowl; no drip, no stream.
5. Inspection window: a little pale batter visible inside the tank's lowest part, just above the tap.
6. Heater switch OFF, its indicator unlit; the plate cold, no glow, no steam.
7. Long handle raised; the stop clip above the lowest unlabelled tick.
Physical inscriptions (render exactly, nothing else): none. No numbers, letters or words anywhere; no quantity marks on the bowl or tank.
Keep clear and visible: the tap grip at frame-left; the swung cup's outer bracket; the bowl base and its contact shadow on the plate; the dry gap below the spout; the hinge joint.
Light: fixed amber work lamp, cool moonlight on brass.
Do not show: the cup under the spout; batter falling; heat glow; writing; a second bowl; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.

Look and finish (same for every ChandRush location plate): premium semi-realistic painterly 2.5D graphic-novel illustration that matches the supplied ChandRush masters, a blend of illustration and reality. It is painterly in finish but crisp and precise in drawing. Materials and light have near-photographic conviction while forms stay clean, idealised and orderly, like a high-end storybook. ChandRush is an ancient travelling fair with grand, mystic, magical scale and real architectural detailing: dimensional deep-indigo and ultramarine painted timber with visible grain, joinery, rivets and edge banding; warm polished and cast brass with bright specular edges and a light patina; pale cream stone worktops and pale irregular stone paving with a light wet sheen and crisp reflections; layered fabric canopies; restrained circular celestial ornament (full-moon discs, rings, small eight-point stars) in gold and brass. Palette: ultramarine, cobalt, indigo and navy against amber, honey-gold and brass, with strong warm-cool contrast, saturated but natural, never neon. Light: fixed amber task lamps cast clean, well-defined warm pools, their glow held tight around the lamp glass with no spreading halo; cool full-moon light edges roofs, canopy gaps, stone and brass; deep, rich shadows that keep readable detail. Clarity: clear, dry night air with no haze, fog, mist, smoke or airborne dust. Crisp edges and high micro-contrast. Sharp, clean textures in wood grain, brass and stone, as in a high-resolution photograph. True deep darks and clean colours, never a milky, washed-out or glowing veil over the image, never soft focus. The background stays crisp and only slightly darker with distance. Ornament is dense above eye level and on frames; floors, worktops and mechanisms stay open, clean and readable.

Production rules (apply to every plate):
- Frame: one 4:3 landscape scenic image filling the whole canvas edge to edge. No border, title band, panel frame, vignette box or blank margin.
- Lettering: the only lettering allowed is the physical inscriptions listed above, rendered exactly as written, letter for letter, with each minus sign as a true minus sign. No other words, numbers or symbols anywhere. No title, caption, callout, label box, leader line, arrow, legend, watermark or signature: titles and callouts are added later by the production team.
- Reference images: their titles, annotation words, label boxes and arrows only identify places for you. Reproduce none of them.
- Empty location: no people, children, helpers, wooden figures, animals, hands, shadows of figures or silhouettes. The place waits, ready for characters to be added later.
- Counts and states are exact as stated. Add no extra copies of any counted object and no extra devices, cards, lamps or tiles.
- Unlit means unlit: clear or smoky glass with no flame, no inner glow and no bloom. Lit lamps glow only at their own glass.
- Avoid: haze, fog, mist, bloom halos, soft focus, a low-contrast or milky wash, modern signage, plastic, neon, sci-fi screens, crowds, text on fabric or banners, mirrored or garbled lettering, duplicated objects, warped or melted geometry, a second moon in the sky, a crescent moon.

Use case: same-camera state change of Image 1 for ChandRush plate L02_F, the dosa dispenser after its portion stop is corrected to one sixth of a kilogram, ready to serve.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image, identical camera to Image 1.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate L02_D. Keep its camera, framing, perspective, architecture, materials, colours, lighting, the dispenser design and every unchanged object exactly.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master, for finish only. Ignore: all white label boxes, annotation words and arrows; cart, bowls, trolley, table.
Change only:
1. Measuring cup: still seated under the tank spout, hinge secured, empty. The sliding brass stop clip on the cup's scale strip moves DOWN to the lowest tick. Beside that lowest tick, on a small cream enamel tag fixed to the scale strip, the inscription "⅙ kg" in bold dark numerals, large enough to read (the tag about one fifteenth of the frame width). The other ticks stay unlabelled.
2. Supply tap: CLOSED, its lever turned across the spout. No liquid anywhere at the spout.
3. Heater: stays ON (the small amber indicator beside the switch lit); the cooking plate surface stays empty, no flame.
4. Dry plate shelf: exactly 6 (six) small round white plates in total, in one row of 6 (six), each separate with gaps, none stacked: the 2 (two) existing plates with the oversized dosa (overhanging its plate) and the tiny dosa stay at the right end, unchanged; add exactly 4 (four) clean EMPTY plates of the same kind to their left. 4 + 2 = 6.
5. On the dry back of the counter, at frame-left, away from the plates: one small brass trial bowl containing a shallow layer of pale cream batter. It carries no writing.
Everything else stays exactly as in Image 1, including the tank (empty), the long handle (raised), the cup outlet (shut), the covered bowls and trays at frame-left, the lamps and the paving.
Physical inscriptions after the change (render exactly, nothing else): "⅙ kg" on the enamel tag beside the lowest tick of the cup scale, fraction with a clean bar. No other numbers, letters or words anywhere; nothing on the trial bowl.
Keep clear and visible: the paving in front of the long handle; the tap grip; the ⅙ kg tag and stop; the shelf edge beside the four empty plates; the heater switch.
Do not show: 5 or 7 plates; plates stacked; batter in the tank or cup; liquid at the spout; the stop above the lowest tick; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.
